name: InsForge Backend Branching
tagline: Git style branching for your backend
description: Git-style branching for your entire backend. Spin off a branch to get a full, isolated copy of everything: your database, storage, auth, edge functions, and more, ready for your agents to experiment on without touching production.
detailed_description: InsForge Backend Branching is a backend isolation and merge workflow that lets developers create a branch of an entire backend environment in seconds. According to InsForge, a branch clones the full backend surface area, including database, auth, storage, edge functions, realtime channels, and scheduled jobs, so changes can be tested without affecting production. The product is designed to replace the risky practice of making backend changes directly on prod with a safer branch-validate-merge flow. InsForge describes branching as an isolated environment where developers can make changes, run dry runs, review SQL, and then merge the result back to the parent environment. It is intended to help teams test schema changes, authentication changes, storage changes, and other backend modifications with less risk. The system also supports conflict detection and resolution when both parent and branch modify the same object, using a merge process that can surface conflicts before applying changes. Overall, it solves the problem of safely experimenting with complex backend systems that are otherwise difficult to clone and merge reliably.[1][2][4]
features: Full backend cloning: creates a branch that copies the backend environment, including database, auth, storage, edge functions, realtime channels, and scheduled jobs, which allows isolated experimentation without touching the original environment.[1][2]

Isolated branch environments: each branch acts as a separate environment where developers can make changes and verify behavior while the parent environment remains unaffected, reducing the chance of accidental production impact.[1]

Dry-run and merge review workflow: InsForge supports a branch workflow where developers can test changes, review the SQL or resulting operations, and only then merge back to the parent, improving safety and change control.[1]

Conflict detection and resolution: if both the branch and the parent modify the same object, InsForge surfaces a conflict and uses merge logic to help reconcile differences before merging, which is important for collaborative backend work.[1][2]

Fine-grained backend merge logic: InsForge says backend branching is not just database-level cloning; it uses object-level and field-level merge logic across backend configuration, which helps preserve valid changes in auth, policies, functions, storage, and related backend settings.[2]
